# Godhajātaka (Ja 141)

**ID:** Ja 141
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1
**Title (Pali):** Godhajātaka
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** The Iguana Who Befriended a Chameleon
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/ja141
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Godhajātaka* (Ja 141) is the opening narrative of the fourteenth chapter (*Asampadānavagga*) in the first book of the Pali *Jātaka* collection [Anandajoti 2010; Fausböll 1877]. Its canonical verse begins *Na pāpajanasamsevī accantasukham edhati* ("He who consorts with evil persons never attains lasting happiness") [Adikaram 1946; Fausböll 1877]. In the commentarial framing, the Buddha delivered this discourse while residing at the Bamboo Grove (Veḷuvana) concerning a treacherous monk who consorted with the hostile faction; the commentary notes that the introductory account (*paccuppannavatthu*) corresponds to that of the *Mahilāmukhajātaka* [Fausböll 1877; SuttaCentral]. In the narrative of the past set during the reign of King Brahmadatta of Bārāṇasī, the Bodhisatta was reborn as an iguana or monitor lizard (*godhayoni*) [Fausböll 1877].

The text preserves an important philological note regarding the transmission of Pali canonical verses: E. W. Adikaram highlights that the Pali *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* explicitly records a variant between the canonical text and the older Sinhalese commentary tradition [Adikaram 1946]. In the verse line *Godhākulaṁ kakanto va kaliṁ pāpeti attānaṁ*, the canonical text read *phalaṁ* in place of *kaliṁ*, but the commentator rejected *phalaṁ* as irrelevant to the meaning [Adikaram 1946].

Regarding parallels and text reuse, SuttaCentral lists four modern translations in four languages but no external parallels in other Buddhist canonical corpora [SuttaCentral]. Automated analysis by DharmaNexus similarly identifies no Pali-internal text reuse and no cross-language matches with a score of 10 or greater [DharmaNexus].
